source_note: Soundgas studio photo of TR-909 #282297 (reference only, (c) Soundgas). Straight-on, 2400x1473 px, 4.50 px/mm. Cross-checked on private/docs/photos/commons_tr909_front_909bd.jpg, private/docs/photos/soundgas/dm_Roland-TR-909-Rhythm-Composer-Drum-Machine-3.jpg, private/docs/photos/commons_tr909_large_bdaniel.jpg, each mapped onto the master by SIFT + RANSAC and dense refinement (tools/panel/crosscheck.py).

sources.name: bdaniel
sources.unit: serial not known (Brandon Daniel, 2009; a perspective-corrected derivative of an oblique shot)

origin: top-left (rear-left) corner of the top view (outer edge of the left side cheek); x right, y towards the player

regularisation.method: rubber-sheeting on straight keylines + 23.0 mm key grid (tools/panel/regularise.py)

frame.decision: regularised (regularise.py, as the first measurement): the master rectified by its outline, then the rubber sheet that puts the dividers on the 23.0 mm key-pair grid and straightens the long bars
why: the printed tick-ring centres fit the small pots of the 1:1 voicing-board artwork to 0.087 mm rms in x on the regularised master, 0.375 mm on the master as rectified
the master's bow is the pattern of a pincushion lens about the picture's middle (lines above it bend up at the ends, lines below it down; sections near the middle narrow, outer ones wide)

the two other straight-on photos (909bd, dm3) show the same pattern with about 60 % of the amplitude (their bars' sagitta -0.5 mm against the master's -0.9), so a homography from them to the master cannot see it: alone it favours k = 0.25, 0.5; with a radial lens term of their own, k = 0.5, 0.75; their own rings miss the pots by 0.229, 0.243 mm rms
the bdaniel photo, perspective-corrected from an oblique view (its distortion lies elsewhere), has the sections regular to 0.1 mm

panel.note: official: 486 (W) x 300 (D) x 105 (H) mm, 4.5 kg (owner's manual p. 39, service notes p. 1)

design_grid.note: step keys at x = key1_x + 23.0*(k-1); instrument sections and step dividers on the key-pair boundaries; small buttons on a 12.0 mm pitch (switch-board artwork)

accuracy: knob centres +-0.1 mm in x, +-0.15 in y (25 pots of the 1:1 voicing-board artwork, SN p. 10: 0.087 / 0.17 mm rms); printed lines, bars, boxes and legends +-0.15 mm relative (three other photos mapped onto the master), +-0.3 mm absolute in the 486 mm frame (+-0.5 within 40 mm of the case ends); raised parts as the photos see them +-0.5 mm (parallax: the file has panel-plane positions); display digits +-0.5 mm; 3-D sizes +-1 mm. See accuracy_table and docs/panel.md.

accuracy_table.evidence: 25 small pots of the 1:1 voicing-board artwork (SN p. 10): 0.087 mm rms, max 0.43 (similarity, 15.725 px/mm); the master as rectified, without the rubber sheet: 0.375 mm
the same pots: 0.169 mm rms (similarity); the page is 1.2 % taller than wide (an affine fit takes it out), the knob rows are 19.86 mm apart on the panel and 20.11 on the page at its x scale

accuracy_table.what: Knob centres against the other photos
Printed lines, bars and boxes, relative
accuracy_table.evidence: dividers and keylines rms x 0.10-0.13, y 0.01-0.03; bars 0.08 / 0.09-0.16; header bars and orange boxes 0.10-0.23 / 0.07-0.08 mm, against two other photos
0.12-0.14 / 0.10-0.15 mm rms, 0.07-0.11 / 0.06-0.08 locally (the legends both photos found alike)

accuracy_table.estimate: +-0.3 mm (+-0.5 within 40 mm of the case ends)
accuracy_table.evidence: the photos still differ from the master by 0.34/0.34 mm (90th percentile) after a homography and a radial lens term, most at the panel ends; the outline sets the frame

accuracy_table.what: Raised parts (key cut-outs as seen, small caps, LED domes)
accuracy_table.evidence: key cut-outs 0.27-0.35 / 0.30-0.37, small caps 0.33-0.34 / 0.29-0.39, scale LEDs 0.34-0.40 / 0.48-0.55 mm rms between photos: each camera leans them differently

fonts.panel_legends: Helvetica Medium caps (Neue Haas / Helvetica). Header bars, step numbers, SHIFT legends and the instrument names in the legend boxes are Helvetica Bold.
fonts.serif: "I" and "II" (BANK) are serif roman numerals (Times Roman).
fonts.logos: Brand marks (roland, tr909, rhythm_composer) are slots only and are never drawn from the photos; fill them from the artwork pack (tr909.svg).

conventions.coordinates: mm from the rear-left corner of the top view (the outer edge of the left side cheek), x to the right, y towards the player; nx = x / panel.w, ny = y / panel.h
conventions.text: bbox = ink bounding box (cap height to baseline for caps-only legends); x, y = bbox centre; cap_h = capital height. Legends printed on a label_box or inside an outline_box are their own text elements.
conventions.label_box: a filled box (header bar, orange box); bbox = its edges; its legend is the text elements inside it
conventions.outline_box: bbox = outer edge of the keyline; points = the keyline's centre line where it isn't a rectangle (the tab over the left key); stroke = keyline width; corner_r = corner radius
conventions.line: points = stroke centre line; stroke = width
conventions.symbol: note glyphs in the scale bars: bbox = the glyph's ink box (head at the lower left, stem up from its right side, one flag on the eighth notes)
conventions.knob: x, y = centre of the printed tick ring (= the pot shaft); knob_d = knob top seen from above; base_d = the skirt; scale = the printed ticks (angles from 12 o'clock, clockwise positive)
conventions.key: x, y = centre of the panel cut-out (photo parallax removed); bbox = the cut-out for the large keys, the visible cap for the small buttons; cap_top = the flat top face; led = the id of the LED element in or behind the cap
conventions.led: led = the tr909::Machine::Led it shows (the processor's snapshot leds[]); shape rect (lens in a key top), round (3 mm LED in a scale bar) or backlight (the centre of a lit small button's frosted window: bbox = that square, window = the window's side)
conventions.display: bbox = the red filter window; digit = the 7-segment module's geometry; the digits are the processor's snapshot digits[] (BCD, 10-15 blank), left to right
conventions.logo: a brand-mark slot: bbox only, never traced shapes; logo = the artwork pack's element id
conventions.param: every interactive element carries param: a knob its parameter id (TR909Processor::knobs(), tempo), a key its tr909::Machine::Key enumerator (Step1 ... EnterAccent), as TR909Processor::setKey takes it

elements.note: top view of the whole unit: 486.0 mm (official width) x 279.5 mm. The depth is the length of the sloping top measured square-on; the official 300 mm depth is the footprint (the base and its front lip reach further forward than the sloping top). Corners rounded r ~1 mm.

rear_panel.source: private/private/docs/photos/soundgas/sn282297_Roland-TR-909-Rhythm-Composer-SN282297-Ed-Obrien-7.jpg (straight-on rear view); cross-checked with Commons RolandTR-909-rear.jpg and the jack-board artwork (service notes p. 12)
rear_panel.note: Seen from behind, so left and right are swapped: x is given in TOP-PANEL coordinates (mm from the left side as seen from the front), y in mm down from the top edge of the rear face. Scale 4.47 px/mm from the 486 mm width. Accuracy about +-1 mm. The rear face is about 97 mm tall (case height 105 mm incl. feet). Legends are dark slate print like the top; MASTER OUT / MULTI OUT have keylines under their titles, EXT CONTROL / TAPE MEMORY/SYNC / MIDI have keylines above their titles, and a bracket joins the two MIDI OUT sockets.

ui_suggestions.note: The 14 middle-row buttons are lit from behind (D618-D631): draw the frosted centre square red/pink when on. The six left-box buttons have no LED.

Positions are panel-plane (base) positions. In the master photo raised parts lean outwards from about (255, 140) mm: key tops by ~1 % of their distance from that point, knob tops by ~2 %. A top-down UI should draw knob caps and key tops centred on these positions (or with a small, consistent fake perspective).
The logo elements are empty slots: the editor draws the marks from the user's artwork pack (tr909.svg in the ROM folder, ids roland, tr909, rhythm_composer) and nothing without one.
